security_audit.summary: All static external command and blocker detections are false positives from Markdown fences and Java examples. No executable shell code or system reconnaissance instruction is present. Two semantic issues remain: logging email addresses and returning rejected input values may expose personal data.

remediation.issue: Logging examples include email addresses in signup and failed login records.
remediation.suggestion: Replace email logging with user IDs, request IDs, or masked values. Use generic reasons for authentication failures.

remediation.issue: Validation error responses include rejected input values.
remediation.suggestion: Omit rejectedValue by default. Only return masked values for an explicit allowlist of safe fields.

content.value_statement: Backend teams often implement inconsistent exceptions, error responses, and logging. This skill provides Spring-style Java patterns for exception classes, global handlers, response DTOs, and service-layer usage.
actual_capabilities: Defines a BusinessException base class and ErrorCode enum for HTTP status mapping.
Shows domain exceptions for not found, duplicate resource, unauthorized, and forbidden cases.
Demonstrates a Spring RestControllerAdvice handler for business, validation, and unexpected exceptions.
Describes an ErrorResponse shape with codes, messages, field errors, and timestamps.
Provides service-layer examples for repository lookup, duplicate checks, authorization checks, and logging levels.
Includes a checklist for reviewing error handling changes.
limitations: Examples are Java and Spring oriented; other stacks need adaptation.
The skill does not run tests or verify framework compatibility.
Project-specific error codes, languages, and response contracts must be defined separately.
Logging examples need privacy review before production use.

use_cases.title: Review Service Error Paths

use_cases.title: Document API Error Contracts
use_cases.description: An API maintainer aligns response fields, status codes, and validation errors across services.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Business Exception
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a new domain error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the allra-error-handling skill to create a BusinessException subclass for a missing invoice in a Spring service. Include the matching ErrorCode entry.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to add validation exception handling for a signup request. Return a standard error response and avoid exposing sensitive input values.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Service Error Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this service method against the Allra error handling standard. Identify missing exceptions, wrong status codes, and risky logging.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an error handling policy for a payment service using the Allra standard. Include exception hierarchy, response format, and logging guidance.

output_examples.input: Create an error handling plan for failed user lookup.
output: Add a user not found exception with a stable not found error code.
Return a standard error response with a clear message and timestamp.
Log the expected miss at warn level without personal data.

output_examples.input: Review a signup service that throws generic runtime exceptions.
output: Replace generic runtime exceptions with domain-specific business exceptions.
Map duplicate email cases to a conflict status and stable error code.
Use structured logging with masked identifiers.

output_examples.input: Define a global exception handler for a Spring API.
output_examples.output: The response should separate business errors, validation errors, and unexpected system errors with clear status mapping.

best_practices: Keep error codes stable and map them to explicit HTTP status values.
Log expected business errors at warn level and unexpected system errors at error level.
Mask personal or secret values in logs and public error responses.
anti_patterns: Do not expose passwords, tokens, or raw rejected values in responses.
Do not concatenate log strings when structured logging is available.
Do not create domain exceptions without a matching ErrorCode.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Java backend services using Spring-style exception handling patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. Teams must adapt names, codes, messages, and tests.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it define every error code?
faq.answer: No. It shows a structure and examples for project-specific error code design.

faq.question: How should validation errors be handled?
faq.answer: Return consistent field errors, but avoid exposing sensitive rejected values.

faq.question: What should teams review before adoption?
faq.answer: Review privacy rules, logging policy, localization, and API response compatibility.
